lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.22 - A Look and learn

details: Look and learn builds recognition of the meaning, form, and pronunciation of want in questions and sentences.
Look for students identifying the correct structure, reading example sentences accurately and repeating want questions and answers with clear form and pronunciation.
“ Do you like studying? Sometimes studying is easy, and sometimes it’s really hard. Let’s learn how to talk about what we want.”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together: 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

lessonPlan.topic: Phonics Book P.114 - A Feed ch- words. Draw lines

details: Feed ch- words and draw lines reviews students’ phonics recognition of ch-words, and reading comprehension. It helps reinforce sound differentiation and word meaning in a structured and fun way.
Look for accurate matching  and clear identification of visuals of ch- words only.
“Mr Monster wants to know what we do at school all day. We tell him we learn new words — ch- words and sh- words! Let’s feed the ch- words to him and practise saying them.”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.

lessonPlan.topic: p116 - C&D Choose words from the story. Write Say the story with friends.

details: Choose, write and say the story reinforces sound recognition, comprehension and spoken fluency in a meaningful context.
Look for confident word choices  to show understanding, good spelling and confident telling of their story to friends.

“Mr Monster loves this story about Chad, Sheena, the chicks, and the yummy lunch. He wants to hear your version of the story too. Let’s choose the correct ch– and sh– words from the pictures, write the sentences, and then tell the whole story to Mr Monster.”
